action: Xbike and Arriva users: treat your email address and trip history as potentially exposed and watch for phishing; Arriva says it is investigating whether anyone besides the researcher requested the data.
date_note: Security.nl published on 19 November; the article gives no date for the flaw itself.
exec: A bike-share platform's access-control flaw exposed users' emails and trips; Arriva says misuse cannot be ruled out.
impact: Email addresses and ride start and end points of Xbike users; spokespersons for both companies told NOS that almost 130,000 users have made at least one ride, of whom more than 40,000 are Arriva customers.
plain: A researcher could pull other users' email addresses and bike trips from the Xbike bike-share app, which Arriva uses. Xbike told the Dutch privacy authority; the app is offline.

sources.name: NOS: Deelfietsplatform lekte fietstochten van gebruikers, ook van Arriva-klanten

summary: NOS reports an anonymous researcher could obtain other users' email addresses and ride start and end points from the Xbike platform because access controls were missing; the leak ran from February 2023, per NOS. Arriva says safeguards were switched off by mistake and misuse cannot be ruled out. Xbike filed a breach notice with the Dutch data protection authority, which confirmed it. The app was taken offline as a precaution.
title: Arriva investigates possible data leak from Xbike bike-share app

validation.note: NOS (original reporting, read) and Security.nl (relays NOS) are one reporting chain; company statements are as quoted by NOS. The authority's confirmation is as NOS reports it. NOS page shows only 'donderdag', no calendar date.

review.note: Compared title, Feb 2023 start, 130,000/40,000 figures, Arriva 'by mistake' statement, AP breach notice, app offline, date 19 Nov against NOS and Security.nl
